newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France, Royal Maroc plan cargo cooper.
newsitem.headline: Air France, Royal Maroc plan cargo cooper.

text.p: A recent draft agreement on a commercial alliance between Air France and Royal Air Maroc(RAM), includes freight cooperation, a cargo official from the Moroccan airline told Reuters.

"A joint committee will consider how we can best co-ordinate our respective freight networks, in order to achieve an efficient use of cargo capacity and ensure the highest possible level of customer service while maintaining our independent structures," the RAM official said.

In a statement, Air France said freight was one of several areas where the two airlines would be looking to develop "complementary synergies to improve service quality and provide a better production cost control."
RAM currently operates a three-times weekly Boeing 737-200F service between Casablanca and Paris.
Air France "wet-leases" 737-200Fs from RAM in operating its own three-times weekly service on the same route.
"The agreement's main objectives are for the two airlines to develop new services either between France and Morocco and further afield," the Air France statement added.

Air France and RAM will also discuss the transfer of the latter's passenger services from Orly to Charles de Gaulle's (CDG) Terminal 2 -- closer to Air France hub installations -- in order to facilitate net work co-ordination, the Air France statement added.
RAM's 737 freighter services between Paris and Casablanca already operate from CDG.
From the 1997-98 winter season the two airlines plan to code-share passenger flights between Casablanca and Lyon and Casablanca-Strasbourg.
Air France has a 3.97 percent shareholding in RAM.
